prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Houston, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1420; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just keep this to the accident itself, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine, though I do need your name for the file. You can give just the first name if you prefer.

A: Okay, it's the claimant, you have it on the form already.

Q: Understood. Can you walk me through where you were heading when the collision happened?

A: I was in the left-turn lane at a signalized intersection in Houston, going to turn left onto the cross street. The light was green for my direction, but the left arrow had not come on yet.

Q: So you were waiting for the arrow to turn left. What did you see next?

A: I started to creep forward into the intersection to get a better view of oncoming traffic. Then I saw a car coming from the opposite direction and I thought I had time. I started my turn and that's when it hit my driver's side front.

Q: Did the other driver have a chance to stop before impact?

A: I honestly don't know. It happened fast. I heard the brakes after I had already committed to turning.

Q: Where do you feel injured?

A: My right shoulder. I hit the door when we spun a little and it's been sore and hard to lift my arm since. I went to urgent care that evening and they took some X-rays.

Q: Have you seen a doctor since then or started any treatment?

A: I have a follow-up scheduled and I'm doing physical therapy exercises at home for now.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you would like to add to your account of the collision?

A: Just that I was trying to be careful, but I know I should have waited for a clearer gap before turning.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
